facts.text: Candler Park is named after Asa Griggs Candler, co‑founder of Coca‑Cola, who donated land for the park in 1922.
The park opened a nine‑hole golf course in 1927, and today it hosts tennis courts, a basketball court, a pool, playgrounds, and wetlands that attract beavers and hawks.
Before becoming a park, area was community of Edgewood, founded in 1870s along the Georgia Railroad and annexed by Atlanta in 1908, sparking Craftsman and Queen Anne homes.
In the late 1860s and 1870s, an African‑American community called Rose Hill emerged within early Edgewood, centered along what is now Candler Park Drive.
Mid‑20th century saw suburban expansion in Candler Park, with modest American Small Houses built in the 1940s and multi‑family dwellings that drew working‑class residents during and after WWII.
